craft_notes: Sthāyin: dispelling graded — universal scope, timed release. Sanskrit-first: sā ca (that-too) kept; jhaṭiti + upāyāntara-prekṣiṇ contrast kept as two destinies (sudden / awaiting). Rows: 5 (long-sweep processional: self-or-world, then dispelling, then the two grades), 9 (suddenly-for-some / awaiting-for-others pair), 1 (‘further means’ closes — the not-yet kept open). Close: 'suddenly for some — for others awaiting further means.' Rejected: resolving the two grades into one — killed: kasyacid/kasyāpi split is the grading; ‘instantly’ for jhaṭiti alone — killed: the pair must stand. Read aloud: HERE — IN the-SELF whose-PITH is-FREE-BLISS, CON-scious-ness a-LONE, OR-ev-ery-WHERE IN the-WORLD as-WELL — THE-con-CEIT of-AD-mix-ING a-noth-er-FORMED re-AL-i-TY is-IM-pu-Ri-ty; THAT, too, is-WASHED-OUT BY-great-BHAI-ra-va-IM-mer-SION: SUDD-en-ly FOR-SOME — FOR-OTH-ers A-wait-ing fur-THER-means.

lines: Here — in the self whose pith is free bliss, consciousness alone,
or everywhere in the world as well — the conceit
of admixing another-formed reality is impurity;
that, too, is washed out by great-Bhairava immersion:
suddenly for some — for others awaiting further means.
l4.sanskrit_cite: tad iha svatantrānandacinmātrasāre svātmani viśvatrāpi vā tadanyarūpasaṃvalanābhimānaḥ aśuddhiḥ sā ca mahābhairavasamāveśena vyapohyate so 'pi kasyacit jhaṭiti bhavet kasyāpi upāyāntaramukhaprekṣī

reads_against.argmap: Where does the admixing-conceit arise, and how is it dispelled? → The conceit defiles self or world alike; mahābhairava-samāveśa removes it — jhaṭiti for the ripe, upāyāntara-prekṣin for the rest.
c1_essence: The conceit of another-formed reality is impurity in self or world alike; dispelled by great-Bhairava immersion — sudden for some, for others awaiting further means.
reads_against.c1_rasa: śānta with vidhi weight (quiescence carrying ritual order)
